A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same selective-SSM generalization study. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support comparison. V2 Appendices A–F correspond to v3 Appendices B–G, with additional material in v3.

before.justification: V2 reports original training-stability and generalization experiments on Majority and IMDb in Section 5 and Figures 1–2.

after.justification: V3 retains these experiments and reports additional ListOps results, parameter-norm training logs in Table 3, and initialization sweeps in Figure 5.

M1.justification: The selective-SSM equations, input-conditioned discretization, parameterization and embedding-plus-single-block architecture are retained. Section 5's broader cross-entropy wording accompanies the added classification task but does not establish a changed proposed procedure.

E1.justification: V3 adds ListOps to both experimental strands in Figures 1–2. Its nested-expression evaluation introduces hierarchical reasoning with single-digit outputs beyond v2's Majority and IMDb binary classification tasks.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates competing models as empirical baselines. Table 1 retains the same theoretical comparisons with linear attention, softmax attention, vanilla RNNs, and discrete- and continuous-time LTI SSMs.

E3.justification: New protocols include ListOps lengths of 100–1000 with ±5 length bands, and a sweep of initial sA from −0.1 to 0.1 in 0.02 increments at fixed Majority/IMDb/ListOps lengths of 250/500/300. Existing state/channel counts and the ten-epoch, 10%-data early-training protocol are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix B.4 adds parameter-norm logs to examine boundedness during stabilization. Appendix B.5 and Figure 5 add controlled initialization sensitivity tests at fixed sequence lengths, extending v2's fixed-sA, varying-length experiment to investigate both stable and unstable initialization regimes.

E5.justification: V2's Figure 2 supplies curves without uncertainty bands or run counts. V3 explicitly reports five random-seed runs, means and ±one standard deviation, and retries failed IMDb seeds until successful runs are obtained. This introduces systematic uncertainty reporting without establishing how many runs underlay v2.

E6.justification: V3 adds ListOps outcomes in Figures 1–2, the training log in Table 3, and initialization-sweep findings in Figure 5. Figure 2 also updates the Majority/IMDb curves to five-run summaries while retaining the broad length-stability trend; their changed aggregation prevents interpreting differences as direct performance gains over v2.

T1.justification: Equation (15) gains the exponent T in its second numerator. New Appendix H derives the finite limit S2 = T(T−1)/2 as rho_A approaches 1. Other proofs and numbered assumptions are retained. Equation (15) still has a denominator sign inconsistent with the appendix formula.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain an attention-based covering-number bound for selective SSMs, a linear-attention corollary, and stability-dependent sequence-length scaling. ListOps broadens the supporting evidence without redefining these claims.

C2.justification: V3 explains why failed training makes generalization gaps undefined, discloses NaN failures even with sA = 0 initialization, and discusses parameter compensation in Appendix B.5. New Section 7 limits applicability to Mamba-style discretization and same-distribution evaluation; Appendix H clarifies behavior at the stability boundary.

D1.justification: V3 documents ListOps preprocessing, vocabulary and length generation, seed-failure handling, and access to additional training logs. The code-access reference changes from an anonymous 4open.science repository to an authored GitHub repository. Existing architecture and training-budget details were already provided in v2.

R1.justification: New Appendix A substantially expands positioning across attention/SSM architectures, PAC-Bayes, information-theoretic bounds, VC dimension and local Rademacher complexity. The introduction and limitations also add relevant attention, initialization and length-generalization work, including Ali et al., Yu et al., and Buitrago and Gu.

P1.justification: Most main-text exposition and existing proof prose are retained. V3 makes localized introduction and experiment rewrites, expands terminology, adds Limitations and Acknowledgments sections, and inserts related-work and discussion appendices while relettering the existing appendices.

P2.justification: Figure 1 changes from a 2×2 to a 2×3 grid. Figure 2 moves from two stacked plots beside text to a row of three panels with uncertainty bands. V3 adds Table 3 and the six-panel Figure 5; the dataset histograms and Table 2 are retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: ListOps, initialization controls, uncertainty reporting and explicit applicability limits improve empirical support and interpretability. These are incremental gains around largely retained theory. The IMDb summaries remain conditional on successful seeds, and the Equation (15)/appendix denominator-sign inconsistency remains unresolved.
